title: Smoke from giant fires is choking the air — here’s a cool trick to clean it!
summary:
Have you ever walked outside and felt like you were breathing through a campfire? That’s what it’s like right now for millions of kids from Minnesota all the way to Virginia. Giant wildfires in Canada and northern Minnesota are pumping so much smoke into the sky that the air has turned a scary purple on pollution maps. Purple means “very unhealthy” — the kind of air that can make you cough, wheeze, or feel sick, especially if you have asthma.

The smoke is full of tiny, invisible particles called PM2.5. They’re so small — about 30 times thinner than a human hair — that they can sneak deep into your lungs. Even tinier ones, called PM0.1, can slip into your bloodstream and reach your brain. Yikes!

But here’s the good news: you can fight back with a homemade air cleaner that costs way less than a fancy store-bought one. All you need is a 20-inch box fan, a good air filter (look for one labeled MERV 13 — that means it catches smoke and germs), and some duct tape. Just tape the filter to the back of the fan, turn it on, and let it suck the dirty air through the filter. Clean air blows out the front!

Some people build a supercharged version called a Corsi-Rosenthal Box using four filters and cardboard. But even the simple one-filter trick can help a lot, says the CDC. Just make sure your fan is clean and not too old, so it doesn’t overheat.

Remember, if you have an air conditioner or heater with a filter, you can also upgrade it to MERV 13. But it only cleans the air when it’s running. So stay inside, keep those fans humming, and breathe a little easier!
why_it_matters: Knowing how to make a cheap air filter lets you protect your family’s health on smoky days, just like wearing a mask when it's dusty outside.
